title: Regional Agreement on Access to Information, Public Participation and Justice in Environmental Matters in Latin America and the Caribbean (Escazú Agreement)
executive_summary: The Regional Agreement on Access to Information, Public Participation and Justice in Environmental Matters in Latin America and the Caribbean, adopted in Escazú, Costa Rica, in 2018 and effective since 2021, is the first legally binding environmental treaty in the region. It guarantees rights to environmental information, public participation in environmental decision-making, and access to justice, emphasizing transparency, equality, and protection of vulnerable groups. The treaty uniquely includes provisions safeguarding human rights defenders in environmental matters. It promotes regional cooperation, capacity-building, and the use of new technologies to enhance environmental governance. The Agreement aligns with global sustainable development goals, aiming to combat inequality and foster sustainable development by integrating environmental protection with economic and social progress. The Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean (ECLAC) serves as the Secretariat, supporting implementation and cooperation among the 33 member countries. This landmark treaty strengthens environmental democracy and accountability, setting a regional standard for sustainable development and human rights protection.
characteristics: The Escazú Agreement is a legally binding regional treaty for Latin America and the Caribbean, adopted in 2018 and effective from 2021, focusing on access to environmental information, public participation, and justice in environmental matters.
It emphasizes human rights, particularly for vulnerable groups and environmental human rights defenders, ensuring their protection and enabling their participation in environmental decision-making.
The Agreement establishes principles such as equality, transparency, non-discrimination, precaution, and intergenerational equity, promoting sustainable development and environmental democracy.
It mandates States to provide timely access to environmental information, facilitate public participation from early stages, and guarantee access to justice with effective legal mechanisms.
The treaty includes provisions for capacity-building, regional cooperation, a clearing house for information, and a Conference of the Parties to oversee implementation and compliance.

It is the first regional environmental agreement to include binding provisions on the protection of environmental human rights defenders and aims to combat inequality and promote sustainable development in the region.

Political Actors: Community of Latin American and Caribbean States

practical_applications: Establishment of a Voluntary Fund to support financing for the implementation of the Escazú Agreement, with contributions from Parties and other sources as defined by the Conference of the Parties.

Creation of a Conference of the Parties (COP) to oversee the implementation and effectiveness of the Agreement, including regular and extraordinary meetings, adoption of rules of procedure, financial provisions, and subsidiary bodies.

Designation of the Executive Secretary of the Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean (ECLAC) as the Secretariat to organize COP meetings, provide capacity-building assistance, and manage administrative arrangements.

Establishment of a Committee to Support Implementation and Compliance as a subsidiary body of the COP to promote implementation, review compliance, and formulate recommendations with public participation.

Development and maintenance of a virtual and universally accessible clearing house on access rights operated by ECLAC as Secretariat, including legislative, administrative, policy measures, codes of conduct, and good practices.

Implementation of national measures by Parties, including legislative, regulatory, and administrative actions, to guarantee the rights of access to environmental information, public participation, and access to justice.
Provision of guidance and assistance to the public, especially persons or groups in vulnerable situations, to facilitate the exercise of access rights.

Guarantee of an enabling environment for persons, groups, and organizations promoting environmental protection, including recognition and protection of human rights defenders in environmental matters.

Establishment or designation of impartial, autonomous entities or institutions to promote transparency, oversee compliance, and monitor the right of access to environmental information, with possible sanctioning powers.

Development of environmental information systems by Parties, including public access to environmental laws, reports, pollutant registers, impact assessments, and other relevant data, updated regularly and accessible through information technology.
Creation and implementation of early warning systems for imminent threats to public health or the environment, with immediate disclosure of pertinent information.

Adoption of mechanisms for public participation in environmental decision-making processes, including early-stage participation, timely and clear information dissemination, and consideration of public observations.

Guarantee of access to judicial and administrative mechanisms to challenge decisions or actions related to environmental information, participation, and environmental harm, including provisions for precautionary measures, evidence facilitation, and redress.

Promotion of capacity-building measures such as training authorities and civil servants, awareness programs for the public and officials, education modules on access rights, and support for vulnerable groups.
Encouragement of regional cooperation and South-South cooperation through workshops, expert exchanges, technical assistance, educational programs, and sharing of good practices.
Encouragement of partnerships with other States, intergovernmental, non-governmental, academic, private organizations, and civil society to implement the Agreement.
Promotion of alternative dispute resolution mechanisms in environmental matters, such as mediation and conciliation.
Parties commit to provide resources for national activities needed to fulfill obligations under the Agreement according to their abilities and priorities.
commitments: The Executive Secretary of the Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean shall convene the first meeting of the Conference of the Parties no later than one year after the entry into force of the Agreement.
The Agreement shall enter into force on the ninetieth day after the date of deposit of the eleventh instrument of ratification, acceptance, approval, or accession.
For each State that ratifies, accepts, approves, or accedes after the eleventh instrument, the Agreement shall enter into effect on the ninetieth day after the date of deposit of its instrument.
The Agreement shall be open for signature from 27 September 2018 to 26 September 2020.

Each Party shall respond to requests for environmental information within a period not longer than 30 business days from receipt of the request, with a possible extension of up to 10 business days in exceptional circumstances.
Each Party shall publish and disseminate a national report on the state of the environment at regular intervals not exceeding five years.

After three years from the date the Agreement has entered into force for a Party, that Party may withdraw by giving written notification, with withdrawal taking effect one year after receipt of notification.

kpi_list.kpi_text: Each Party shall respond to requests for environmental information as quickly as possible and within a period not longer than 30 business days from the date of receipt of the request, or less if so stipulated in domestic legislation.
kpi_list.metric_name: Response Time to Environmental Information Requests
kpi_list.target_description: Respond to environmental information requests within 30 business days or less
kpi_list.measurement_method: Tracking response times to information requests

kpi_list.kpi_text: Each Party shall take steps to establish a pollutant release and transfer register covering air, water, soil and subsoil pollutants, as well as materials and waste in its jurisdiction. This register will be established progressively and updated periodically.
kpi_list.metric_name: Pollutant Release and Transfer Register Establishment
kpi_list.target_description: Establish and periodically update a pollutant release and transfer register covering key environmental pollutants and waste
kpi_list.measurement_method: Existence and periodic updating of pollutant registers

kpi_list.kpi_text: Each Party shall publish and disseminate at regular intervals, not exceeding five years, a national report on the state of the environment.
kpi_list.target_description: Publish and disseminate a national environmental report at least every 5 years
kpi_list.measurement_method: Publication and dissemination records of environmental reports

kpi_list.kpi_text: Each Party shall ensure that the competent authorities respond to requests for environmental information within a period not longer than 30 business days, with a possible extension of up to 10 business days in exceptional circumstances.
kpi_list.metric_name: Maximum Extension Period for Environmental Information Requests
kpi_list.target_description: Allow extension of response time by up to 10 business days in exceptional cases

kpi_list.kpi_text: Each Party shall guarantee an enabling environment for the work of persons, associations, organizations or groups that promote environmental protection, by recognizing and protecting them.
kpi_list.metric_name: Enabling Environment for Environmental Protection Actors
kpi_list.target_description: Recognize and protect persons and groups promoting environmental protection
kpi_list.measurement_method: Legal and policy frameworks supporting environmental defenders

kpi_list.kpi_text: Each Party shall create and strengthen national capacities, based on its priorities and needs, including training authorities and civil servants on environmental access rights and raising public awareness.
kpi_list.metric_name: Capacity Building for Environmental Access Rights
kpi_list.target_description: Create and strengthen national capacities through training and awareness programs
kpi_list.measurement_method: Number and quality of training and awareness programs implemented

kpi_list.kpi_text: The Executive Secretary of the Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean shall convene the first meeting of the Conference of the Parties no later than one year after the entry into force of the present Agreement.
kpi_list.metric_name: Timing of First Conference of the Parties Meeting
kpi_list.target_description: Convene first Conference of the Parties meeting within one year after Agreement enters into force
kpi_list.timeframe: within 1 year after entry into force
kpi_list.measurement_method: Date of first meeting relative to entry into force date

kpi_list.kpi_text: Each Party shall ensure that the rights recognized in the present Agreement are freely exercised.
kpi_list.metric_name: Guarantee of Free Exercise of Access Rights
kpi_list.target_description: Ensure free exercise of rights to access information, public participation, and justice in environmental matters
kpi_list.measurement_method: Legal and practical assessments of rights exercise

kpi_list.kpi_text: Each Party shall establish or designate one or more impartial entities or institutions with autonomy and independence to promote transparency in access to environmental information, to oversee compliance with rules, and monitor, report on and guarantee the right of access to information.
kpi_list.target_description: Establish or designate autonomous entities to oversee transparency and compliance in environmental information access
kpi_list.measurement_method: Existence and functioning of oversight institutions

kpi_list.kpi_text: Each Party shall promote, where appropriate, alternative dispute resolution mechanisms in environmental matters, such as mediation, conciliation or other means that allow such disputes to be prevented or resolved.
kpi_list.metric_name: Promotion of Alternative Dispute Resolution Mechanisms
kpi_list.target_description: Promote mediation, conciliation, and other alternative dispute resolution methods in environmental matters
kpi_list.measurement_method: Availability and use of alternative dispute resolution mechanisms

extra_data.responsible_entity: Executive Secretary of the Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean
sdg_alignment: SDG 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions

top_actors.name: Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean (ECLAC)
top_actors.justification: ECLAC is the primary institutional actor responsible for the Secretariat functions of the Escazú Agreement, organizing meetings, providing assistance, and publishing the Regional Agreement. It is prominently mentioned throughout the document as the key regional UN body facilitating the treaty's implementation and cooperation.

top_actors.name: United Nations
top_actors.justification: The United Nations is the overarching international organization under whose auspices the Escazú Agreement was adopted and deposited. The Secretary-General acts as Depositary of the treaty, and the UN framework and principles (e.g., Rio Declaration, Sustainable Development Goals) are foundational to the Agreement.

top_actors.name: Governments of Latin America and the Caribbean
top_actors.justification: The governments of the 33 countries in Latin America and the Caribbean are the Parties to the Agreement, responsible for ratification, implementation, and compliance. They negotiated, adopted, and are expected to enforce the treaty provisions, making them central actors in the document.

top_themes.name: Multilateralism (Regional & International Cooperation)
top_themes.justification: The document centers on the Regional Agreement on Access to Information, Public Participation and Justice in Environmental Matters in Latin America and the Caribbean, a legally binding multilateral treaty adopted by multiple countries. It emphasizes regional cooperation, collective action, and the role of multilateral institutions like ECLAC and the UN, making multilateralism the core theme both in content and strategic importance.

top_themes.name: Environmental Rights and Access to Justice
top_themes.justification: A major focus of the document is guaranteeing environmental rights, including access to information, public participation, and justice in environmental matters. This theme is central to the treaty’s objectives and commitments, addressing vulnerable groups, human rights defenders, and sustainable development, thus strategically critical for the region.

top_themes.name: Digital Governance (Data & Governance)
top_themes.justification: The Agreement highlights the use of new information and communication technologies, open data, and environmental information systems to facilitate transparency and access to environmental information. While important, this theme is more a tool or enabler within the broader multilateral and environmental governance framework, with less content dedicated compared to multilateralism and environmental rights.
